source: ...I'll bet someone in this castle knows something.
Farewell, King Hamlet. I'll find that book. At the very least, I have a theory on where to begin.
Yes. The Book of Fates. I remember our discussion.
I've found it. The only question is what to do with it.
Is there some unfinished buisness holding you back from making a choice?
Do not turn away from this oppertunity, Ophelia.
My best lead is that Simona is still alive. She's the last person who had the book.
I'm doing my best to find it, but I don't know where to begin looking.
If only Astrid was still alive, or haunted these walls as I, we could ask her.
Someone has to know something. I'll keep looking.
What do you know of a strange, cursed book?
A... cursed... book?
My apologies, my dear girl. You must have me mistaken for someone else.
I bring quilts, clothing for babes. I am merely an old woman who wishes to love God and enjoy the joyful silence of a life well lived.
I know nothing of any sort of books. Never had a mind for them.
(She's acting so peculiarly.)
My King, I have reason to believe Lady Simona is alive. What do you know of her?
I haven't heard that name in...
How? Can that be... possible?
No... certainly not.
She may be living nearby, in town. Again I ask, what do you know of her?
She was my father's consort. All knew of her presence. She was there when my mother died.
I never asked my father about her... it simply isn't done. But... I assumed... she had passed, too.
Thank you for this information, Ophelia. I'll consider it further.
My Queen, I have reason to believe Lady Simona is alive.
Alexander's woman? But she passed away years ago.
A-at least, I'd presumed as much... I wasn't living at Elsinore then. I was still in Bohemia.
I'm afraid I don't know much about her. But even if she were alive, she'd be a very old woman by now.
Father, I have reason to believe Lady Simona is alive.
Lady Simona? Goodness, where did you hear that name?
No, my dear, I'm afraid not. She's buried in the graveyard. I recall that much at least. Her grave is there, if you'd like to visit.
Irma, do you think Lady Simona is alive? I have reason to believe she is.
Simona? I've scarcely heard that name. You do mean the Lady Simona?
The same one.
I never crossed paths with the woman. Gerta and I came to Elsinore after she had already perished.
There's a grave for her in the yard. You believe it to be empty?
Then this is a thread which presents too much danger for an old woman like me to be interested in pulling it.
Me, I stick to my drink and my cards and my cuisine, thank you!
Hamlet, I have reason to believe Lady Simona, your grandfather's consort, is alive.
What do I care of old women and older men? Naught but bones now.
But... if she left the castle, aren't you concerned about why? Where did she go? And why won't anyone speak of her?
I've never concerned myself with it. I observed my father and Claudius to be discomfited by her name as a boy.
There's a grave for her in the graveyard. But of course, it's fake.
It's... fake?
One of the gravekeepers told me, when I grew a little older. They'd buried an empty coffin.
Wherever Simona's flown, it's somewhere far away...
I have reason to believe Lady Simona, Alexander's consort, still lives.
I'm quite familiar with her, yes.
An obnoxious woman, isn't she?
I'll have to find a nice death for her, in time.
Yes, something wonderful to repay her kindness in keeping my book from me for so long!
Perhaps I'll go and pluck her eyes out with my fingers. Or saw out her tongue with a shard of glass!
You know, I've spent entire game matches doing nothing but dismembering my opponent.
I remember a particular young man whom Zeus asked me to punish for stealing a flame...
Yes, I took out his liver each morning, and it grew back each night!
They say Hercules freed him, but that's a hopeful lie. He died in utmost agony.
Quite a lively performer, that one. Most excellent outlook. Disappointed me greatly, in the end.
I'm afraid she's long gone from this game board.
She exists outside of my reach. Not even I could find her now.
Ah, but as to whether she's alive...
I'm certain the answer is yes. Please do let me know if you find her.
Your father's consort is still alive, but not in Elsinore. What became of her?
It wasn't spoken of in my lifetime.
Even Claudius and I have never passed her name between us. She... my mother...
Terrible, bloody deeds were committed. My father was a cruel and greedy man.
I do not know her whereabouts, but if she left Elsinore, she must have passed through town.
<i>But I am confined to these walls. I may not leave the board's edges.
I know who you are. You're Lady Simona.
No one's ever called me a lady, lass...
But you are. You're King Alexander's former consort. I'm Ophelia. You knew my mother, Elise, didn't you?
You're the exact image of her.
But Lady Simona died a long time ago. You're too late.
She wanted nothing to do with that cursed, vile castle or any of the evil people dwelling within it.
And I still don't. Good day to ye, lady. May no harm come to you.
Or do you have some business with me I should be aware of?
I... found my mother's diary. It spoke of you. I know about your time in the castle. And I think you found something, didn't you?
You still have that cursed book within your possession.
I would assume you were mad, but I know your mother's face well. You have so much of Elise in you.
Not any longer. It wandered off from my personal items three days ago.
It has gone on to ruin some other poor soul's life.
(I see. She doesn't have it any longer because it's sitting in my bedroom.)
(So this, too, is an item that exists outside the timeline.)
Do you know the power vested within this book?
It's... just a blank book.
Its pages are not blank for me.
It contains the many thousands of fragments of worlds I have seen. Of futures that never came to pass. Of pasts that never were.
I know precisely what you mean, and I'm here to put an end to it.
I need the Book to prevent time from repeating itself.
My child, I am afraid you have been lied to.
The one causing your world to repeat isn't the Book of Fates. It's Peter Quince.
No. that can't be true. Quince is the one who asked me to find the Book. He helped me find you. Why would he do that?
That vile man... when I heard rumors that King Hamlet was searching for a particular book, I suspected Quince was behind it.
He knows I am weak. Though I will never return the Book to him, I may give it to another one of his poor victims.
His 'victims?' What are you saying?
I've never told this story before. It is the story of my greatest sin.
Many years ago, I was fated to die by Queen Astrid's hand.
She resented my relationship with her husband. She wanted me dead.
One night, while sleeping, I felt someone slit my throat in the darkness. I bled to death there, in my bed. It should have been the end. But it wasn't.
Because I woke up. And I was alive once more.
Quince found me shortly afterwards. He seemed to know everything about my circumstances immediately. I grew comfortable speaking with him.
This sounds painfully familiar.
And then he proposed a game of sorts.
He offered me the Book and promised me that if I used it, I could change fate, like a god. In return, he offered to make time repeat, giving me infinite opportunity.
He made just one thing clear: the Book was his, and his alone. Once I had gotten my revenge and used it, it would return to his hands.
And so I explored every alley, every pathway of my world. He followed me eagerly, curious to observe every choice I made.
I could have kept the both of us alive, Astrid and me. But I didn't. I was a woman spurned, and I was out for blood and the crown.
Instead, I used the Book of Fates to have her driven mad. I wanted to be Queen. You know the story.
And Quince helped me bring that world about. I saw how he took such glee in the horrific weeks which followed. My life became a living hell, one I'd created for myself.
Ophelia, have you noticed that this world spins ever constantly towards disaster?
I'd never known my family and friends to be capable of violence like this.
Surely you aren't saying that Quince is the one who makes them act this way?
No. Their demons are truly theirs. But he has some ability to impose his will upon the world, to influence it. I'm certain you've witnessed it. And he enjoys that power.
That disgusted me. I realized I had been used for his pleasure, that I had sold my friends and family for the sake of the power he'd offered me.
The morning after Quince freed me from my game with him, I chose a new path.
I knew I had to convince him to give me the book once more. In the end, it wasn't hard. He is an artist, and all artists can be played through their vanity.
I told him I wanted to learn from the Book, to learn to be like him. He indulged me by granting it to me once more-- of course he did.
And I ran for my life. I fled, and I hid. And the years passed in that silence.
And Quince never came for you?
He knew I wouldn't grant the Book to him. But he well knows I shall give it to you now.
What? If what you say is true, why would I ever want it?
Because he will never let you leave your repeating world and die in peace. Not until you've used its powers, and it has returned to his hand. He made that mistake with me.
I hoped that when I died, the Book's power would simply die with me. But he knows me well. And he knows I would never allow Elise's daughter to suffer in infinite hell.
He knows I loved your mother like my own flesh and blood. Very well, then. May this be my final gift to her.
If you don't make the Book's power your own, the only world available to you will be whichever future Quince makes for you.
So... if I use this Book, I can determine the fate of this world?
To an extent. People are people. You cannot create a fate which is impossible for broken people to achieve.
